pairingScope: Same process, same round, same complete manifest and seeds; all configured warmups and rounds required.
parityScope: Every measured reference and optimized best snapshot, best/final RMSE and best epoch; optimizer/shuffle parity is covered by tests.
limitations: Qualification applies only to each compatible protocol/engine/backend/worker group; different hosts are never pooled.
Warmup-only outcomes are retained separately and excluded from measured timing/parity distributions.
Within-engine numerical parity does not establish cross-engine or cross-host arithmetic equivalence.
Per-trial phase timings overlap across models and place boundary scoring differently on CPU versus CUDA.
Raw JSONL byte hashes retain provenance; complete parsed round records can be reconstructed from this artifact without the raw files.
Smoke has one warmed process per engine/backend and one measured round per case; do not derive speedups, latency distributions or performance qualification from it.
CPU REFERENCE first warmup differs on eight trials from earlier warmed outcomes; full divergent round data is retained. This artifact establishes warmed measured continuation only.

One measured CUDA REFERENCE trial changed from prior SESSION dispatch to COHORT. Its same-case arithmetic matches exactly, but there is no strictly matching route/device metadata precedent in the earlier nine measured rounds.
This 2,000-epoch fixed-work smoke does not qualify the separate 1,000,000-epoch reliability protocol.
Source revisions are launcher/report declarations; process exit and matching provenance are verified, but the harness does not emit independent compiled-class hashes.

smokeValidation.scope: Final-source correctness continuation only; one warmed JVM fork and one measured round per case cannot qualify timing.
smokeValidation.comparisonRule: Match exact case (engine/backend/execution/workers/searchSeed), topology and training seed to all nine earlier measured rounds. Report stricter complete device/route metadata matching separately. Warmups never count as measured evidence.
